// Tests for the bounded receive-only tunnel queue patch; MIT, see LICENSE.
package quic

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"

	"github.com/quic-go/quic-go/internal/utils"
	"github.com/quic-go/quic-go/internal/wire"
)

func TestTunnelDatagramRingBoundsAndRelease(t *testing.T) {
	q := newDatagramQueue(func() {}, utils.DefaultLogger)
	c := &Conn{datagramQueue: q}
	frame := &wire.DatagramFrame{Data: make([]byte, 4)}
	for cycle := 0; cycle < 3; cycle++ {
		for i := 0; i < maxDatagramRcvQueueLen; i++ {
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(frame.Data, uint32(cycle*maxDatagramRcvQueueLen+i))
			q.HandleDatagramFrame(frame)
		}
		q.HandleDatagramFrame(frame)
		n, b, d := c.DatagramReceiveQueueStats()
		if n != maxDatagramRcvQueueLen || b != 4*n || d != uint64(cycle+1) {
			t.Fatalf("stats %d %d %d", n, b, d)
		}
		for i := 0; i < maxDatagramRcvQueueLen; i++ {
			data, err := q.Receive(context.Background())
			if err != nil || binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data) != uint32(cycle*maxDatagramRcvQueueLen+i) {
				t.Fatalf("FIFO/copy failed %d %v", i, err)
			}
		}
		for _, payload := range q.rcvQueue {
			if payload != nil {
				t.Fatal("popped payload retained")
			}
		}
	}
	if n, b, _ := c.DatagramReceiveQueueStats(); n != 0 || b != 0 {
		t.Fatal("accounting leak", n, b)
	}
}

func TestTunnelDatagramByteBudgetAndFullQueueNoAllocation(t *testing.T) {
	q := newDatagramQueue(func() {}, utils.DefaultLogger)
	frame := &wire.DatagramFrame{Data: make([]byte, 65535)}
	for i := 0; i < maxDatagramRcvQueueBytes/len(frame.Data); i++ {
		q.HandleDatagramFrame(frame)
	}
	before := q.rcvSize
	if allocs := testing.AllocsPerRun(100, func() { q.HandleDatagramFrame(frame) }); allocs != 0 {
		t.Fatal("full queue still allocates", allocs)
	}
	if q.rcvSize != before || q.rcvBytes > maxDatagramRcvQueueBytes || q.rcvDrops == 0 {
		t.Fatal("byte budget ignored")
	}
}
